item.title: UX-06 : mention sur les données personnelles du questionnaire
item.body:
## Issue
Closes #630
Claim: mac/ux06-opus

## What and why
UX-06: the personal data notice of the user survey, in French, in `docs/ux/questionnaire/donnees.md`. Status: all PO decisions of 2026-11-08 are applied (V1–V7, D3 revised to 10, ownership of the pseudo texts), and so is the Fable cross-review (M1–M5, L1–L4, nitpicks). The PO still has to validate the final text.

- §1: the paragraph above the optional pseudo field `I1` (asked at the end, D2), and the list of facts that the short texts in `questions.md` (#667) must state. `questions.md` owns the field label, the help text and the link label; `donnees.md` owns the facts, this paragraph and the detailed page.
- §2: the detailed page:
  - controller and contact (Bruno Arene, ezzz75@gmail.com) and purpose;
  - data recorded, aligned with the spec #668: answers and card order, free texts, pseudo kept apart, date without time, time spent, survey version, token hash, IP hash;
  - what stays in the browser, and what is not collected (no IP in logs, no cookie, no audience measurement, no third-party request);
  - who sees what: Bruno alone sees the pseudos; the other developer and the AI assistant (a third-party online service) see only a pseudonymised copy; the host has technical access only; Tailscale (Funnel relay) sees the IP and connection metadata but not the answers, and may be outside the EU;
  - where data lives (France; only pseudonymised extracts go to the AI service, which may process them outside the EU);
  - retention: IP and token hashes plus the salt are erased at closing; pseudos, the mapping table, all answers and all analysis copies two months after closing;
  - rights: access and copy, correction, erasure, withdrawal, objection and restriction, with a one-month delay and an honest caveat for answers without a pseudo; CNIL; legal basis.
- §3: the consistency table with `cadrage-construction.md` §4, which is unchanged, plus the requirements for #633.
- §4: the PO decisions.

Dates and the threshold are config placeholders (`{date_fermeture}`, `{date_effacement}`, `{seuil_statistiques}`, `{date_mise_a_jour}`).

### Requirements for the form spec #633 (not guaranteed by §4)
- R1: server and proxy logs never contain the IP in any form (neither plain nor hashed).
- R2: no cookie at all; the token and the draft are in local storage.
- R3: the draft is erased after a successful submission.
- R4: the IP and token hashes are never exported; the salt is destroyed at closing; the rate-limit hash stays in memory.
- R5: `{date_effacement}` is computed as closing + 2 months, with no separate setting (a manual earlier erasure stays possible, hence « au plus tard »); the dates and the threshold come from the config and are shown by the page.
- R6: an automatic erasure at `{date_effacement}` of all answers, pseudos and the mapping table, plus a documented procedure for backups and analysis copies (the other developer's copy included).
- R7: a command to find, show, correct or erase the answers of one pseudo, which also gives its analysis identifier so that copies can be fixed.
- R8: the detailed page is served by the form and opens without losing the draft.
- R9: the analysis copy is pseudonymised: a random identifier (not the internal SQLite id), and a mapping table that stays on the server only.
- R10: free texts of the analysis copy can be edited before analysis without touching the stored answers, with a trace of the edits.
- R11: an aggregate-only export for publication (closed questions, no free text, identifier, time spent or card order), no figure for a question or group of fewer than 5 respondents; it is the only data kept after erasure.
- R12: no audience measurement, client-side or in the logs (no IP, user agent or referrer).
- R13: a « limitée » flag keeps an answer stored but out of stats, later analysis copies and the R11 export (restriction, objection).

R4 also keeps the salt and the hashes out of backups, and R5 forbids postponing the closing date after the first answer (CodeRabbit threads, commit e5d8350d).

### PO decisions (all taken 2026-11-08)
V1 the pseudo only serves to contact by private message to dig into a topic · V2 pseudos erased two months after closing · V3 answers erased at the same date · V4 pseudonymised before any AI analysis · V5 no free-text excerpt published · V6 VPS in France · V7 one-month delay · D3 threshold of 10.

**PO to confirm**: the Tailscale Funnel wording (decision of 2026-11-09, commit 29766a09). Also new and changeable: R11's minimum group of 5, and the phrase "l'autre développeur de l'app" naming who may read the pseudonymised copy.

## How it was verified
- `npx -y markdownlint-cli2@0.18.1 docs/ux/questionnaire/donnees.md`: 0 errors.
- Each promise was cross-checked against `cadrage-construction.md` §4 (the §3 table of the file); the ones §4 does not cover are R1–R13 above.
- The data list was checked against `formulaire-spec.md` on `docs/ux09-spec` (#668), and the short-text facts against `questions.md` on `docs/ux05-questions` (#667).

## Checklist (AGENTS.md §9)
- [x] Module boundaries respected (docs only)
- [x] Tests added/updated: n/a, docs only
- [x] No secrets; fixtures anonymized
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Author model: Opus 5.5 / Reviewer model: Fable 5.1
- [x] Fixes or changes a legacy-app behaviour? No

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — If pre-closure backups retain the hashes and secret key, the potential exposure encompasses backed-up respondents in this questionnaire, not merely one response. These controls constrain normal handling but leave pre-closure copies subject to R6's later deadline. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Specify a closure owner and closure-time treatment of every pre-closure backup containing hashes or key material. Revised after the Fable cross-review and the PO decisions of 2026-11-08 (commit 0732a8b4). Lint: 0 errors.

**Fable findings**
- **M1**: the notice now says "pseudonymisée" while the mapping table exists, explained in plain words. Readers get no direct identifier. The hosting sentence became "stockées en France" with no contradiction: only pseudonymised extracts go to the AI service, which may process them outside the EU. R9 says "pseudonymisée côté serveur".
- **M2**: "l'équipe" is gone. Bruno alone sees pseudos and the stored answers. Only the pseudonymised copy may be read by "l'autre développeur de l'app" and by the AI assistant, named as a category ("un service en ligne d'une société tierce").

- **M5**: following the PO ownership rule, §1 keeps only the paragraph above the field and lists the facts the short texts of `questions.md` must state. Label, help and link label are owned by #667.
- **L1**: added objection and restriction, plus receiving a copy (portability) for pseudo holders.
- **L2**: "anonymes" is replaced with "rien ne permet de vous identifier, sauf ce que vous écririez vous-même dans un texte libre".
- **L3**: the host is listed (technical access only).
- **L4**: §3 now says §4 does not guarantee "no audience measurement"; new R12 covers it.
- Nitpicks 1–5 are applied: the stale line on pending PO points, R1–R12 in the PR body, "aucune police téléchargée", the rate-limit hash computed in memory, and R4 now says which backups it covers.

- R5: `{date_effacement}` is computed from the closing date.
- After erasure only the aggregates remain; browser leftovers are mentioned.
- Rights can be exercised in the analysis copies through R7.
- R11 publishes no figure for a group under 5 (new; the PO can change it).

**PO decisions**
- D3: §3 now says 10; the page uses `{seuil_statistiques}`.
- C08 is not mentioned in the notice.

**For #667**
- I1 help and E0 still say "vos réponses (restent) sont anonymes". Per L2 the facts list suggests "sauf ce que vous écririez vous-même dans un texte libre". The one-month delay and "deux mois après la fermeture" are also facts the short texts should state. Copied in the shared notes for the UX-05 session.

**Gaps still in #668 (for the spec author, not changed here)**
- R5: no erasure date or substituted placeholders.
- R6: `reponses` is never erased, which contradicts the two-month erasure.
- R7: no per-pseudo command.
- R9: the export carries the SQLite `id`, not a random identifier with a mapping table.
- R10, R11 (small-group rule) and R12 are not in the spec.

Not merged.

_Posted with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) for the PO (Bruno)._

Aligned with the second Fable review of the spec #668 (commit 62745ed6). Lint: 0 errors.
- **Free-text fields**: the data table now lists the current four free-text fields in plain words: G1 (what annoys you day to day), L2 (what matters most when reading a topic), C11 (another idea), F1 (closing free field). « ce qui vous manquerait » is gone, and C08 is not mentioned.
- **Erasure date**: `{date_effacement}` is still closing + 2 months, with no separate setting. Since the spec keeps a manual earlier erasure, the notice now says « au plus tard le {date_effacement} » in the paragraph above `I1`, the retention table and the rights section. R5 and R6 say the same.
- **R1**: reworded to match the spec: no IP in server or proxy logs in any form, neither in plain text nor hashed. The notice sentence « Les journaux techniques du serveur ne contiennent pas votre adresse IP » already matched.
- **R11**: now « une question ou un groupe de moins de 5 répondants », matching the spec's per-question minimum.
- The PR body is updated to match.

Not merged.

_Posted with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) for the PO (Bruno)._

Tailscale Funnel exposure (PO decision 2026-11-09) added in commit 29766a09. Lint: 0 errors.
- **Qui voit quoi**: a new bullet names Tailscale (Tailscale Inc.) as the service that relays connections to the server. It sees the IP address and connection information (time, volume) but not the answers, because the connection stays encrypted up to the server and Tailscale cannot decrypt it. What it keeps of that metadata follows its own rules, not this survey's.
- **Où sont les données**: the connection passes through Tailscale relay servers, which may be outside the EU, and stays encrypted there.
- **Ce qui n'est pas collecté**: the IP line now says the Tailscale relay does see the IP pass, so « no IP kept » only covers what this survey controls.
- §4 records the decision, and the PR body is updated (Tailscale, R13 from the CodeRabbit fixes).

**PO to confirm the wording**, in particular « ce qu'il garde relève de ses propres règles ». I did not check Tailscale's retention policy, so the notice makes no promise about it.

The review threads are left to the PO. Not merged.

## Adversarial review of `docs/ux/questionnaire/donnees.md` (UX-06, #630)

**Verdict: ready after minor fixes.** Every PO decision of 2026-11-08 is stated correctly (controller and contact, optional pseudo at the end used only to contact a participant, pseudos and all answers erased two months after closing, aggregates only kept, anonymisation before AI analysis with the mapping table on the VPS, no published free-text excerpt, VPS in France, one-month delay, no IP beyond anti-abuse, no cookie, no audience measurement). The French is plain and readable by a forum user. The findings below are wording and completeness fixes; none reverses a decision. The bigger risk is downstream: PR #668 does not yet implement most of the R-list, so several promises in this notice are currently kept by nobody (see "Gaps in #668").

I checked against: issue #630, `cadrage-construction.md` §4 on `dev-swift`, `formulaire-spec.md` on `docs/ux09-spec` (#668), `questions.md` on `docs/ux05-questions` (#667). I am not a lawyer; the GDPR points are flagged for the PO to weigh, not legal advice.

**M1. "Anonymisé" is pseudonymisation while the mapping table exists, and the EU hosting sentence contradicts the AI sentence** (lines 84–89, 94, 96, R9 line 158)
For Bruno the analysis export is pseudonymised (GDPR art. 4(5)): the pseudo↔identifier table lets him re-link it, so it stays personal data on his side. What the AI service receives has no direct identifier and no key, which is the honest claim to make. Separately, line 94 says "Aucune donnée du questionnaire n'est hébergée hors de l'Union européenne" and line 96 says the AI service "peut se trouver hors de l'Union européenne": a reader who sends free text will read these as contradictory. Fix: keep plain words but make them exact. Line 94: "Vos réponses sont stockées en France, dans l'Union européenne." Line 96: "Seules des réponses sans pseudo ni détail permettant de vous reconnaître peuvent être envoyées à l'assistant d'intelligence artificielle, dont le service peut se trouver hors de l'Union européenne." In §3/R9 (internal), say "pseudonymisé côté serveur, sans identifiant direct côté assistant" so #633/#635 do not inherit the loose term.

**M2. "L'équipe qui développe l'app" is an undefined recipient and clashes with "Bruno est le seul"** (lines 81, 83, 94)
Line 81: only Bruno sees complete answers. Lines 83 and 94: free texts and exports stay "au sein de l'équipe qui développe l'app". Line 34: "projet personnel". A respondent cannot tell who that team is; in this project it is the AI agents, which the notice already describes separately as "un assistant d'intelligence artificielle". Fix: either drop "l'équipe" and keep two recipients only (Bruno; the AI assistant, anonymised), or define it in one clause ("c'est-à-dire Bruno et les assistants d'IA qu'il utilise"). Also name the category of the AI recipient ("un service en ligne d'une société tierce") so the recipient category is stated; the author already asked the PO this question in the PR comments, it needs an answer before merge.

**M3. Server-side token and server logs are missing from the data and retention tables** (lines 56, 72, 100–108)
Line 56 says the token is recorded "À l'ouverture du questionnaire", which contradicts line 53 ("Rien n'est enregistré sur le serveur avant Envoyer"): at opening it exists only in the browser; the server receives it at send and, per #668 §5.3, keeps a hash of it in `jetons` until closing. The retention table has a row for the browser token but none for the server copy. Line 72 promises no IP beyond anti-abuse but says nothing about access logs, while R1 (line 150) tolerates plain IP in proxy logs for 7 days. Fix: line 56 "Quand" → "Créé dans votre navigateur à l'ouverture, envoyé avec vos réponses"; add a retention row "Jeton (copie sur le serveur) | {date_fermeture}"; add one sentence under "Ce qui n'est pas collecté": "Les journaux techniques du serveur ne contiennent pas votre adresse IP" and make R1 strict (no plain IP at all, which is what #668 §9 and §11 already specify), or keep the 7-day fallback and say it in the notice.

**M4. Data table does not match what #668 stores** (lines 53–58)
Line 58 lists "La date et l'heure d'envoi" to spot bursts; #668 §5.3 stores the date only (`recue_le` AAAA-MM-JJ), which cannot spot bursts. #668 also stores `duree_s` (time taken, 0–7200 s) and `ordre_cartes` (card order), neither listed here; the duration is behavioural data about the respondent and belongs in the table. Fix: one of the two documents must move. Suggested: notice says "La date d'envoi (sans l'heure)" and adds a row "Le temps passé à répondre | À l'envoi | Vérifier que le questionnaire tient dans le temps annoncé"; `ordre_cartes` can be covered by a clause in the first row ("et l'ordre dans lequel les cartes vous ont été montrées").

This PR: field label « Pseudo HFR », help « Indiquez seulement votre propre pseudo. », E0 link « Vos données : ce qui est gardé et pourquoi ». #667 `I1` Aide: « Facultatif. Sans pseudo, vos réponses restent anonymes. Si vous en laissez un, vous pouvez demander à tout moment qu'il soit supprimé : écrivez à Bruno Arene, ezzz75@gmail.com. Le détail est dans la mention sur les données. »; #667 `E0` ends with « Lire la mention sur les données. ». Fix: decide the owner once. Suggested: `questions.md` owns the question label and help (it is what the concordance test reads), `donnees.md` owns only the paragraph above the field and the detailed page; then either drop lines 19 and 23 here or mark them "proposition pour #629, `questions.md` fait foi", and have #667 add "Indiquez seulement votre propre pseudo" to its help.

**L1. Rights list lacks objection, restriction and portability** (lines 112–116)
Line 125 bases the non-pseudo data on legitimate interest, which carries a right to object (art. 21); the pseudo is on consent, which carries portability in principle. Access, rectification, erasure, withdrawal, CNIL are present. Fix: add one plain bullet "à vous **opposer** au traitement de vos réponses, ou à en demander la **limitation**" and keep the honest caveat that without a pseudo nothing can be found. Not a lawyer; the PO may judge portability irrelevant for a 20-question survey, but objection should be there.

Free text can contain self-identifying details, and an IP fingerprint plus a date exist until closing. Fix: line 15 "Sans pseudo, rien dans vos réponses ne permet de vous identifier, sauf ce que vous écririez vous-même dans un texte libre." Line 119 is already honest; keep it.

"Personne d'autre : rien n'est vendu, prêté ni transmis" ignores the VPS host, which has technical access to the machine. V6 removed the `{hebergeur}` placeholder; a category is enough. "No third-party domain" does not by itself exclude self-hosted audience measurement or server-side visit statistics. #668 §9 (logs without IP, UA, Referer; no cookie) is what actually makes the promise true. Fix: add R12 "Aucune mesure d'audience, ni côté client ni dans les journaux (pas d'adresse, d'agent utilisateur ni de référent)" and point #635 at it.

1. Line 9: "Les points qui attendent le PO sont regroupés à la fin" is stale now that V1–V7 are settled; say "Les décisions du PO sont consignées à la fin".

Covered by the spec as written: R1 (§9 no IP in logs, §11 proxy without IP, §13 asks the PO; stricter than R1), R2 (§4, §9), R3 (§4 draft erased after accepted send), R4 (export columns exclude the fingerprint; `sel` erased at closing §12), R8 (`GET /donnees` §7, draft in `localStorage`).
